$comment: Claude's own opening selections for Matchweek 5, written and committed to disk before Codex's blind run for this gameweek (protocol.md). Same discipline as MW4: probability written down before edge computed, not revised after seeing the resulting edge size. Large edges (double-digit points) from this qualitative method are flagged, not quietly trusted -- see per-selection notes.
estimate_method: Qualitative, form-and-injury-adjusted probability estimate: recent-form base rate adjusted for home advantage and the specific injury/availability news gathered for each side. Not a fitted statistical model -- same caveat as MW4.

selections.reasoning: Chelsea missing Caicedo, Henderson, Emegha, Satpaev, Palestra but retain squad depth. Brentford missing captain Nathan Collins (calf). Both drew 2-2 in MW4.

SUPERSEDED pre-lineup text kept for the record: 'Tottenham missing Kudus, Maddison, Solanke, Simons (long-term ACL), Odobert -- an unusually deep attacking-injury list for a side already blunt (0-0 v Everton in MW4). Villa also missing Bailey, Abraham, Onana, Gomes, Manzambi, but Tottenham's absences look more attack-critical.' Revised 2026-09-19 after the official confirmed lineup (tottenhamhotspur.com, corroborated by spurs-web.com and lastwordonsports.com): Solanke -- the specific striker assumed missing -- STARTS for Tottenham, with Kudus and Maddison fit enough to be named substitutes; only Simons (confirmed long-term ACL) and Odobert are genuinely absent now, not five players. Villa: Gomes (returning from suspension, not injury) and Manzambi (full debut) START, with Abraham (brace v Coventry in the cup) among the substitutes; only Bailey and Onana are genuinely absent. Both sides recovered far more of the assumed-missing personnel than modelled, which narrows -- doesn't reverse -- the asymmetry the original pick leaned on (Tottenham's absences 'more attack-critical' than Villa's). Tottenham getting its first-choice striker back is, if anything, the single biggest specific change and nudges the balance a little further towards Tottenham/draw. But per the standing process lesson from Brighton-Arsenal (CLAUDE.md): a personnel headline is only decision-relevant if it's new relative to what the team has actually shown -- Tottenham have not scored in the Premier League in four games this season under various lineups, and Villa have scored only once in four, so the underlying attacking output for both sides has been poor regardless of who's nominally out. That tempers how far this should move the estimate. Net: probabilities shifted modestly (home_win 0.40->0.42, away_win 0.31->0.29, draw unchanged at 0.29), not dramatically -- reasoned independently of the price, then checked against it.
selections.price_source: oddschecker.com (Bet365 line via racingpost.com, explicitly attributed to bet365)
selections.decision_reason: edge clears 3pp threshold, but only just -- down from +5.7pp at the original (unconfirmed-lineup, stale-price) estimate to +4.0pp now. This is thin enough, and sensitive enough to how much weight is put on the lineup revision above, that it is flagged as a borderline call for the owner rather than presented as a clean holdover.
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: Official confirmed lineup (tottenhamhotspur.com 'Confirmed Line-ups: Spurs vs Aston Villa', corroborated independently by spurs-web.com and lastwordonsports.com) checked ~1hr pre-kickoff (KO 11:30 UTC). Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Robertson, van Hecke, Tonali, Savio, Fernandes, Solanke, Marmoush, Pedro Porro, Bentancur, van de Ven (c); subs include Maddison and Kudus. Villa XI: Suzuki, Lindelof, Mings, McGinn (c), Kamara, Buendia, Jackson, Ruggeri, Wan-Bissaka, Gomes, Manzambi; subs include Abraham. See reasoning field for the full comparison against the pre-match assumption and the revised probability.
selections.head_to_head_note: Checked 2026-09-19, owner-prompted. Villa have won 4 of the last 5 meetings between these two sides (3 May 2026: Villa 1-2 Spurs was the exception; before that Spurs lost the Jan 2026 FA Cup tie, the Oct 2025 league meeting, and two 2025 fixtures, all to Villa). CORRECTED after discussing with Codex: this was initially logged as supporting evidence for the pick, which overstates it. Codex's pushback, applied here: 'automatically adjusting for four wins in five is much less defensible [than a genuine lineup change] -- investigate whether a repeatable tactical explanation survives changes in managers, players and venue' before treating it as evidence at all. No such mechanism was checked (has the manager changed since those results? the squad has turned over substantially). Five matches is a small sample in the same spirit as the Arsenal 6-0-0 sample being too small to call 'crisis-proof' in the other direction. Recorded as background only, not counted as supporting evidence in the edge/decision above -- the taken decision rests on the lineup-check and current-form reasoning alone.

selections.reasoning: SUPERSEDED pre-lineup text kept for the record: 'Both sides missing significant attacking options -- goals harder to come by for either side than the market's 57.7% fair BTTS-yes implies.' Revised 2026-09-19: the same lineup check as the match-result entry shows both sides recovered far more attacking personnel than assumed (Solanke starting; Kudus/Maddison on the Tottenham bench; Gomes/Manzambi starting and Abraham on the bench for Villa), which weakens the specific 'missing attackers' mechanism the original BTTS-No case rested on. Weighed against that: both teams' actual scoring output this season has been poor regardless of personnel (Tottenham yet to score in the league in four games; Villa one goal in four), which is real evidence for a low-scoring game independent of who's nominally out, per the standing lesson to check actual results, not just a headcount. Net: probability moved from 0.52/0.48 to 0.50/0.50 -- a modest, not dramatic, revision -- reasoned before checking the resulting edge.
selections.price_source: oddschecker.com (Bet365 line) -- COULD NOT be freshly re-confirmed as a Bet365-specific quote today despite repeated attempts (oddschecker's BTTS page returned 404/blocked content); retaining the last-confirmed Bet365 price. Cross-book BTTS-Yes prices checked today (Betfred 1.67, William Hill 1.62, Matchbook 1.76, Coral 1.65, Ladbrokes 1.65, BetMGM -172) cluster close to the 1.615 implied by this original market, so there is no evidence of a material price move -- but this is a real sourcing gap, flagged rather than papered over.
selections.decision_reason: edge clears 3pp threshold even under the revised, more conservative probability (+7.7pp, down from +9.7pp)
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: Same official confirmed lineup as the match-result entry above (tottenhamhotspur.com, corroborated by spurs-web.com and lastwordonsports.com). See that entry's actual_lineup_check_note for the full XI, and this entry's reasoning field for the revised BTTS view.

selections.reasoning: SUPERSEDED -- see correction_note. Original text: 'Arsenal missing three first-choice central defenders at once (Mosquera, Timber, Saliba) -- a genuine defensive crisis for the league's best defence, not a minor absence.' This was wrong: treated season-long, already-priced-in absences as fresh news and never checked Arsenal's actual results with this lineup situation.
selections.decision_reason: reasoning_error -- caught by the owner, not the process. Arsenal are 6 wins from 6 in all competitions this season, including matches missing this same back-three combination: Saliba out long-term since before the season got going (targeting ~21 Nov return), Timber recovering (expected back around the first international break, so already out for most of the wins), Mosquera out 3 games (hamstring vs Aston Villa, also during a run of wins). None of that is a fresh 'crisis' -- it's the status quo the team has already won through repeatedly. Declined because the premise was factually wrong, not because the edge (+3.44pp) was disliked or adjusted to fit a result. No revised pick issued -- would need a proper re-analysis weighing recent form/results alongside injuries, not just an injury list read in isolation.
selections.correction_note: Verified 2026-09-15 via Arsenal.com and other outlets. This is now a standing process lesson (see CLAUDE.md): weigh recent form/results with the current lineup situation, not just a raw injury list, before calling any absence pattern a 'crisis'.
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: Official confirmed lineup (arsenal.com, 'Team news: Mosquera starts away to Brighton'): Raya; Timber, Mosquera, Gabriel, Hincapie; Zubimendi, Rice; Eze, Saka (c), Martinelli, Gyokeres. Only Saliba is out -- Timber and Mosquera, the other two 'missing centre-backs' the original (declined) reasoning leaned on, both start. This directly reinforces, rather than reopens, the standing correction: not only was the 6-0-0 record already evidence the absence pattern wasn't a fresh crisis, today's actual team news shows two-thirds of the assumed absentees are playing anyway. No re-analysis performed here -- this fixture remains declined; there is no revised probability to price, since the decline was never about the price.

selections.reasoning: Everton defensively tight (0-0 v Tottenham in MW4). Ipswich in good early form (won on return to the top flight, cup win) with minimal injuries. Landed close to market's own fair split.
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: No material team-news surprise: Everton have Tarkowski and Branthwaite back from being rested (fit, as this candidate assumed); Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil says the squad has no injury crisis beyond the long-standing absence of Jack Taylor. This candidate (draw, 0.0272 edge) remains declined -- edge_below_threshold, unaffected by today's lineup check.

selections.reasoning: Newcastle carrying an unusually severe injury list -- Dan Burn, Joelinton, Jacob Ramsey, William Osula, Nico Gonzalez, Ewen Jaouen and Anthony Elanga all out, including both club captain and vice-captain. Hull drew 2-2 away at Chelsea in MW4, a credible result for a promoted side. Shaded down from the market's heavier Newcastle favouritism given the scale of the absences.
selections.price_source: oddschecker.com (Bet365 line), refreshed 2026-09-19 ~1hr pre-kickoff (Newcastle 3/5, Draw 10/3, Hull 4/1 with Bet365)
selections.decision_reason: edge clears 3pp threshold. Note: Hull win also clears the threshold independently (+3.11pp at the original price) but is not taken separately -- one candidate per market, per established convention, and Draw carries the larger edge.
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: Official confirmed Newcastle lineup (insidefutbol.com, published 13:48 BST): Hornicek; Miley, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, Willock; Murphy, Barnes, Fernandez-Pardo, Wissa. All seven originally-modelled absentees (Burn, Joelinton, Ramsey, Osula, Nico Gonzalez, Jaouen, Elanga) remain out, and Nico Gonzalez's absence is now confirmed for a specific reason (concussion protocol from the 4-1 defeat at Leeds) rather than the general knock originally assumed -- a genuinely new fact, and if anything it reinforces rather than undercuts the discount already applied to Newcastle. No unmodelled return of a key absentee. Edge recomputed against today's Bet365 price (draw shortened slightly from 4.50 to 4.333): +4.14pp, still clears the 3pp threshold. Selection continues to hold; not yet placed by the owner as of this check.

selections.reasoning: Coventry still bottom, still barely scoring, and now missing suspended top scorer Taiwo Awoniyi on top of the existing injury list (Wright, Kesler-Hayden, Eccles, Woolfenden).
selections.decision_reason: edge_implausible_model_uncertainty -- a 15.3pp gap from an unvalidated qualitative method is in the same range as MW4's Coventry-Brighton BTTS situation, which was declined on the same ground. The suspension is a real, specific catalyst, but the magnitude is still more likely to reflect an overweighted qualitative read than a genuine mispricing. Declined outright, not conditionally -- consistent with not revising a position after seeing how large the edge turned out to be.

selections.reasoning: Both sides carrying several absences (Bournemouth: Araujo, Kroupi, Adli, Milosavljevic; Liverpool: Bradley, Leoni, Ekitike, Chiesa, Gomez doubtful). Landed close to the market's own fair split -- no differentiated view.
selections.decision_reason: edge_below_threshold -- still below the 3pp floor even at today's slightly shorter Liverpool price (+1.04pp, up from -1.14pp at the original price, but nowhere near threshold). Also a genuine standing disagreement with Codex's higher probability estimate (0.56 vs our 0.44), not a data gap.
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: Official confirmed lineups (lastwordonsports.com), checked ~1hr pre-kickoff. Bournemouth and Liverpool both fielded exactly the absentee lists this candidate's reasoning assumed (Bournemouth: Araujo, Kroupi, Adli, Milosavljevic all out; Liverpool: Bradley, Leoni, Ekitike, Chiesa all out) -- no material surprise. Recomputed at today's refreshed Bet365 price (Liverpool 2.20, was 2.05): edge is +1.04pp, still well below the 3pp threshold. Remains declined; no conclusion bet, regardless of what this check found, per standing instruction (this is a real disagreement with Codex's own higher probability estimate, not a lineup or pricing gap).

selections.reasoning: Leeds coming off a morale-denting 4-1 home defeat to Newcastle in MW4, still missing Rodon and Joseph. Palace has its own injury list (5 out per Squawka) but no specific detail found. Shaded Leeds down slightly from the market's favouritism given the heavy loss last time out.
selections.price_source: oddschecker.com (Bet365 line), refreshed 2026-09-20 ~1hr pre-kickoff (Leeds 7/10, Draw 3/1, Palace 15/4 with Bet365) -- Leeds shortened from 1.833 to 1.70 since this file's original run
selections.decision_reason: edge_below_threshold -- more negative than at the original price (-10.08pp, was -5.19pp), since Leeds has shortened further
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: SERIOUS SCRUTINY APPLIED PER OWNER INSTRUCTION, 2026-09-20 pre-kickoff. Official confirmed lineups (lastwordonsports.com, corroborated by insidefutbol.com): Leeds out Harry Wilson (quad) and Joe Rodon (hamstring), with Ilia Gruev back available -- broadly consistent with or slightly better than this candidate's assumption. Crystal Palace out Dean Henderson (GK) and Jean-Philippe Mateta, their first-choice striker, both until after the international break, plus Axel Disasi suspended -- Palace materially weaker in attack than a generic 'has its own injury list' framing suggested. None of this supports reviving Leeds home_win (already declined on Claude's book): Leeds now priced even shorter (1.70) than at research time, pushing our own edge further negative. Decline reinforced on both team-news and price grounds. Codex's own candidate for this fixture is a different selection (away_win/Crystal Palace, declined separately on reasoning_error grounds -- see requests/rejected-selections.json) -- no overlap, no conclusion bet possible either way.

selections.reasoning: Man City heavily favoured at home; Sunderland missing Alese plus a long list flagged as on international duty (treated with some scepticism -- 20 September is not a standard FIFA window date, so this may be a stale search result; the underlying view that a newly-promoted Sunderland away at City is a plausible City-clean-sheet scenario stands regardless).
selections.price_source: oddschecker.com (Bet365 line) -- 'Both Teams to Score - No' quoted at 1/1 (2.00) with Bet365, refreshed 2026-09-20 ~1hr pre-kickoff, up from 1.80. A clean Bet365-attributed BTTS Yes price to pair with it could not be independently confirmed today; fair probability below holds this market's original overround (0.0684) constant and applies it to the new No price only -- flagged as an estimate, not a freshly observed two-way market.
selections.decision_reason: edge clears 3pp threshold; already flagged at selection time as a larger-than-typical gap (was 10.0pp, now 15.2pp under the estimated-overround method) -- moderate-to-high, monitor rather than auto-decline, since the underlying logic (heavy favourite at home vs newly-promoted side) is a more standard pattern than MW4's Coventry outlier
selections.actual_lineup_check_note: Official confirmed lineups (lastwordonsports.com), checked ~1hr pre-kickoff. Man City XI: Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Semenyo; Haaland -- Phil Foden out (suspended, red card), already covered by the general 'missing Alese plus a long list' caveat in this candidate's own reasoning; Haaland returns from a midweek rest to lead the line, a modest positive for City's attack that, if anything, argues for MORE City goals and doesn't disturb a BTTS-No case built on Sunderland's defence, not City's attack. Sunderland XI: Roefs; Mukiele, Ballard, Danso, Methalie; Xhaka, Sadiki; Le Fee, Meunier, Angulo, Brobbey -- Reinildo suspended, Habib Diarra (hamstring) and Romaine Mundle (long-term knee) both out. One source flags a Riquelme Angulo as 'unavailable' while the confirmed lineup lists an Angulo starting -- an unresolved discrepancy between sources, noted rather than silently resolved, and immaterial to the BTTS view either way. This session's original caveat about 20 September not being a standard FIFA international window is now moot -- the confirmed absences above are club-specific (injury/suspension), not international-duty related. No material surprise. Price has moved in the bettor's favour (1.80 -> 2.00); edge recomputed at +15.19pp under the estimated-overround method described above, up from +10.0pp. This is a real, placed-pending conclusion-book position (see ledger/conclusion.json, already placed at owner price 1.70) -- treated with the care that implies. Still subject to methodology.md section 7's 19 September BTTS systematic-bias flag; this is a pre-existing (2026-09-15) selection being rechecked, not a new one, so the pause on new BTTS picks does not apply to it.
